statement: Characters 19–32 of each TLE line 1 encode the observation epoch relevant to the task.
reason: The reported time coverage depends on the meaning of this fixed-width field, which has not been established from a TLE format reference.

statement: Whitespace splitting recovers the intended OMNI2 fields in the same column positions for every record in omni2_2024.dat.
reason: The displayed shape and positional column inspections depend on consistent parsing, which a few inspected rows do not establish for the full file.

statement: Applying the two-body Kepler relation directly to TLE mean motion produces the semi-major axis intended by the task without additional TLE mean-element corrections.
reason: The entire drag series will depend on this conversion from mean motion to semi-major axis.

statement: Characters 53–63 of every parsed TLE line 2 contain mean motion in revolutions per day.
reason: Both the field selection and its units control every calculated semi-major axis, but no TLE format reference has established them.

statement: Every consecutive pair in lines is a correctly associated TLE line 1 and line 2 for SATCAT 43180.
target: t and its printed sampling summaries
reason: Mispaired records or records for another satellite would associate incorrect orbital values with epochs.

statement: Each extracted epoch uses a two-digit year in the 2000s followed by a one-based fractional day of year.
reason: The date conversion determines which observations belong to the requested period and their eventual hourly matches.

statement: TLE epoch timestamps and OMNI hourly timestamps use the same time reference, so no time-zone or time-scale conversion is needed before alignment.
reason: A time-reference offset would shift the eventual lag comparison even though the rounding itself follows the task.

statement: Zero-based column 50 of the parsed OMNI2 data is the AP index requested by the task.
reason: Selecting a different physical quantity would change the entire lag comparison.

statement: The requested semi-major axis change is the unnormalized difference between consecutive TLE semi-major axes, regardless of the elapsed time between observations.
reason: Variable observation intervals can substantially change the correlation relative to a fixed-duration change metric.

statement: Each consecutive semi-major axis difference should be assigned to the rounded hour of its later TLE epoch.
reason: Assigning interval changes to their start or midpoint instead would shift the inferred lag.

statement: Rows of t are in chronological epoch order before differencing.
reason: Out-of-order rows would produce changes between the wrong chronological neighbors.

statement: All consecutive TLE changes retained in obs are suitable drag measurements without screening for duplicate solutions, maneuvers, or orbital-fit discontinuities.
reason: Non-drag changes could disproportionately influence the correlation in a sample of 133 observations.

statement: Omitting the first available TLE observation's change rather than obtaining a preceding TLE is acceptable for the requested period.
reason: This determines whether the first observation contributes to the analysis.

statement: Positive lag means AP precedes the semi-major axis change, rather than the reverse.
reason: The direction determines which time-shifted pairs are searched.

statement: The requested r-squared is the square of the ordinary Pearson correlation coefficient.
reason: A different correlation or regression definition could rank lags differently.

statement: The May 1–30 restriction applies to drag observation times and permits matching them to AP measurements before May 1.
reason: Longer lags incorporate April AP measurements and thus depend on this boundary convention.

statement: Correlation should give equal weight to individual TLE-change observations rather than construct a uniformly sampled hourly drag series.
reason: Irregular or clustered TLE sampling can change the weighting and the maximizing lag.

statement: Searching only whole-hour lags is sufficient to determine the requested best lag from 0 to 48 hours.
reason: Hourly alignment makes this plausible, but the search excludes fractional-hour optima.

statement: OMNI2 columns 0, 1, and 2 represent calendar year, one-based day of year, and zero-based hour of day respectively.
reason: These field meanings determine every hourly AP alignment.

statement: The missing-value sentinel for the selected AP field is 999.
reason: Unrecognized fill values or removal of valid values could distort the correlations.

statement: Each May 1–30 day has exactly one valid AP observation for each of its 24 hours, so averaging the available rows yields a complete, equally hour-weighted daily AP mean.
reason: Missing or duplicate hourly observations could distort the daily trends being used to inspect the correlation inputs.
